title: Record and inspect Cell command usage
summary: Register systems and commands, append invocation observations through the shared Rust API, and report recorded activity by system, command, thread and time.
use_when: Registering command identities during installation, recording a product command boundary, or inspecting recorded usage.
do_not_use_when: The requested result is token accounting, command output, domain success or an inferred execution tree.
outcome: An append-only record of observed command invocations or a scoped report of those records.
effects: Explicit registration initializes only an empty Chancery usage journal and inserts system/command identities.
Recording appends one observation for a registered command; reports select existing rows. CLI report dispatch can append its own observation.
authority: Chancery owns the journal, registration and reporting interpretation. Each product owns instrumentation and domain success.
success: Registration is retained or the selected usage insert commits. Reporting returns selected recorded observations and explicit zero-use commands; none establishes product success or exhaustive coverage.
failure_and_recovery: Recording returns an error after bounded SQLite contention; the observe adapter emits a bounded diagnostic and preserves the product command result.
No automatic append retry, migration, update, delete or pruning. Preserve compatible private backups and database-local cursor scope.
privacy: Retains only opaque system, command and optional Codex thread identities, invocation IDs and observation times in a private current-user database. No arguments, credentials, output, model context or network disclosure.

interfaces.label: Report recorded invocations
interfaces.invocation: chancery usage commands [--system SYSTEM] [--thread THREAD] [--since UNIX_SECONDS] [--until UNIX_SECONDS]

interfaces.label: Read observations
interfaces.invocation: chancery usage events [--thread THREAD | --unattributed] [--after ID] [--limit COUNT]

consumers.statement: Local product CLIs and explicit library callers record command boundaries; operators register identities and query usage.

preconditions.statement: Recording requires an initialized supported private journal and registered system/command pair. Registration can initialize an empty journal. Direct service calls supply request-scoped thread identity.

inputs.statement: Stable system and command IDs, optional CODEX_THREAD_ID or explicit thread, absolute optional CHANCERY_USAGE_DB, and system/thread/time/page query filters.

outputs.statement: Registration results or Chancery schema-three report envelopes with system identities, per-command counts and latest selected times, or insertion-ordered events with next_cursor and has_more.

data_semantics.statement: Each usage row observes one command-handler entry, regardless of its later outcome. Registration and usage are append-only. Zero counts describe selected recorded observations only.
The journal does not report token consumption, outcomes, duration, command content, verified thread identity or parent-child execution relationships.

identity_and_units.statement: System ID is global; command ID is unique within system. Usage ID orders local inserts. recorded_at and time filters are whole Unix seconds. Missing thread is NULL. IDs are opaque 1–128 byte ASCII metadata.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Queries select committed records at the read boundary. Since is inclusive and until exclusive. Counts include registered commands with zero selected usage; recording failures, disabled recording and uninstrumented boundaries remain uncovered.
No exhaustive command coverage, missed-observation count or historical retention horizon is promised.

access.statement: The local Rust API and CLI use a private regular SQLite file; current-user filesystem permissions are the trust boundary. No daemon or network surface exists.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Initialization accepts only empty or schema-one Chancery state. Registration is idempotent and may partially commit before an error. Each append is a separate insert with a foreign key. Database triggers reject updates/deletes. No automatic retries or migrations.

operational_limits.statement: SQLite busy timeout is 100 ms. Event page limits are 1–1000, default 100. CHANCERY_USAGE_DISABLED=1 suppresses dispatch observations only. No durable queue or output capture exists.
No hard wall-clock latency, throughput or database-capacity objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Journal schema one, crate version, provider release and capability version are separate. Unsupported journals fail; products do not migrate them. Historical identities remain after program removal.

reliances.statement: The journal is local Chancery-owned state. Recording a supplied Codex thread ID performs no Codex lookup or runtime invocation.
